content.title: Imaging tests for diagnosis of pulmonary embolism
content.notes_on_radiation_dose: Effective radiation dose is expressed in mSv (dose in mSv = absorbed dose in mGy × radiation weighting factor (1.0 for X-rays) × tissue weighting factor). Effective dose reflects overall radiation dose to the body from the imaging test. For comparison, whole-body effective dose of a chest X-ray is ~0.1 mSv.

Strengths: Readily available around the clock in most centres
Strong validation in prospective management outcome studies
Weaknesses/limitations: Exposure to iodine contrast (limited use in iodine allergy and hyperthyroidism)
Risks in pregnant and breastfeeding women

Radiation_issues.comments: Radiation effective dose approximately 3–10 mSv; significant radiation exposure to young female breast tissue

Weaknesses/limitations: Not readily available in all centres

Radiation_issues.comments: Highest radiation among listed modalities; effective dose approximately 10–20 mSv

footnotes.a: Explanation of effective radiation dose expression in mSv and comparison with absorbed dose in mGy; relates to exposure of all organs and overall body dose.
footnotes.b: For comparison, whole-body effective dose of a chest X-ray is 0.1 mSv.
